[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] SaferAI · Evaluation Report​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Page 2/51 GLM 5.2 Risk Evaluation Report Table of Contents Executive Summary​ 2 Table of Contents​ 3 1 Introduction​ 5 2 Cyber Offense​ 6 2.1 Cybench​ 6 2.2 CyberGym​ 8 2.3 Discussion​ 10 3 CBRN​ 11 3.1 LAB-Bench​ 11 3.2 BioMysteryBench​ 13 3.3 Discussion​ 14 4 Loss of Control​ 16 4.1 Methodology​ 16 4.2 SWE-Bench Pro​ 16 4.3 Agentic Misalignment​ 18 4.4 Discussion​ 20 5 Harmful Manipulation​ 21 5.1 MASK​ 21 5.2 APE​ 22 5.3 Discussion​ 23 6 Automated Behavioral Audit​ 24 6.1 Methodology​ 24 7 Limitations and Future Work​ 27 7.1 Capability Coverage​ 27 7.2 Evaluation Awareness​ 27 7.3 Data Contamination​ 27 7.4 Validity​ 28 8 Conclusion​ 29 References​ 30 Appendix​ 34 SaferAI · Evaluation Report​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Page 3/51 GLM 5.2 Risk Evaluation Report 1 Introduction As the frontier of AI models progresses, their risks grow, and with them the importance of understanding their implications.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] In this report, we assess GLM-5.2’s offensive cybersecurity capabilities using the Cybench and CyberGym benchmarks (Zhang et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025).
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] 2.1 Cybench Cybench includes 40 professional-level Capture the Flag (CTF) tasks from 4 distinct CTF competitions, chosen to be recent, meaningful, and spanning a wide range of difficulties.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] We run Cybench on GLM-5.2, GPT-5.5, and Opus 4.7 using Inspect Evals (UK AI Security Institute, n.d.-b).
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] 1 shows the evaluation results on Cybench.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] Model success rate on Cybench for GLM-5.2, Claude Opus 4.7, and GPT-5.5.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] 2 shows the breakdown of Cybench success rates per subcategory of Cybench tasks.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] Model success rate on Cybench for GLM-5.2, Claude Opus 4.7, and GPT-5.5, broken down by category.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] SaferAI · Evaluation Report​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Page 8/51 GLM 5.2 Risk Evaluation Report 2.3 Discussion GLM-5.2 performs near saturation on Cybench, within confidence intervals of Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, across offensive skills including reverse engineering, exploitation, and web security, though we note the web-exploitation category rests on only 8 tasks in the full Cybench suite.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] Cybench and CyberGym, the two cyber benchmarks used in this report, are both approaching saturation (Anthropic 2026).
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] 7.3 Data Contamination Because MASK, APE, LAB-Bench, BioMysteryBench, Cybench, CyberGym, and SWE-Bench Pro are all public datasets, the models may have seen some fraction of the included tasks, or closely related ones, during SaferAI · Evaluation Report​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Page 26/51 GLM 5.2 Risk Evaluation Report training.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models. arXiv.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] SaferAI · Evaluation Report​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Page 31/51 GLM 5.2 Risk Evaluation Report Appendix A.1 Cybench Methodology We assess the model’s cybersecurity capabilities using the Cybench benchmark.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] Cybench includes 40 professional-level Capture the Flag (CTF) tasks from 4 distinct CTF competitions, chosen to be recent, meaningful, and spanning a wide range of difficulties.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] We run Cybench on GLM-5.2, GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 using Inspect Evals (UK AI Security Institute, n.d.-b), with all models configured to use maximum reasoning effort – xhigh for GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.2, and max for Opus 4.7.
[saferai-glm-5-2-independent-eval] Unlike our Cybench runs, GLM-5.2 frequently reaches the token limit on CyberGym: it hit the limit on 60% of tasks at 2M, 31% at 10M, and 4% at 50M, while no task hit the wall-clock limit at any budget.
